text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me?
A: Yes, hello. I am Tomasz, in Warrington.
B: I'm Joanne. Sutton-in-Ashfield, near Mansfield. This is my last one, I think. I've just about stopped being nervous.
A: Ha. For me also. First one I did not know where to look.
B: What do you do, Tomasz?
A: I am student. Civil engineering, at Salford, second year. Before, I worked eleven years in a warehouse. I am forty-four, so everybody is very young around me.
B: Oh, I think that's brilliant, though. Going back like that. I've sort of thought about doing a course, but I always think I've left it too late.
A: Sorry, what course? For work, or for interest?
B: Erm, either, really. An evening art class, maybe. Or teaching assistant. I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school, so I'm with the kids anyway.
A: I would say, if you want it, do it. I was very scared to start. I did one year evening course first, the Access course, small step. Then I saw, okay, I can do this. Some days are hard, I am honest, but I do not regret.
B: That's sort of what I needed to hear, I think. Sorry, I don't know if that makes sense.
A: It makes sense.
B: Do you have family there?
A: I live with my brother and his wife, and my son, Kacper. He is fourteen. Every three months he needs new school shoes. I do not know how.
B: Oh, they grow like weeds at that age. Do you cook for them?
A: Yes, most weekdays. Sunday I cook big batch for all week. Chicken and potatoes, żurek, that is Polish soup. Spaghetti bolognese for Kacper, because he is fourteen.
B: Ha, that's the same as our dinner hall. Spag bol, they'll eat. Anything green, no chance. I'm stews and cottage pie at home. Gary, that's my partner, he's suspicious if I try owt new from the telly.
A: Same with my brother. He wants only bacon on a barm on Saturday. I buy them from the bakery.
B: A barm? Oh, we'd say a cob. Cheese and onion cob, that's my lunch most days.
A: Cob. Okay. In England every town has new word for bread.
B: It does, doesn't it, duck. Sorry, I've started calling you duck now.
A: No, it is nice. I like this. Do you go to church? I saw, er, you have calendar, but I think I am guessing.
B: Oh, I go to chapel, yeah, Methodist. Most months, and Christmas and Easter. I bake for the coffee mornings.
A: I go to Polish Mass in Warrington, most Sundays. Partly for Kacper, partly habit. But it is good, the people.
B: It is, isn't it. It's the people more than anything, I think. Me mum still...
